message.content:
Let Fresh’s volume be \(V\) and its price be \(P\).  
Since Fresh costs \$1.00 per unit volume,

\[
\frac{P}{V}=1.00
\]

Glow has \(33\frac13\% = \frac13\) more volume than Fresh, so

\[
V_{\text{Glow}}=\frac43 V
\]

Bright costs \(60\%\) more than Fresh, so

\[
P_{\text{Bright}}=1.6P
\]

Glow is \(25\%\) less expensive than Bright, so

\[
P_{\text{Glow}}=0.75 \times 1.6P = 1.2P
\]

Thus Glow’s cost per unit volume is

\[
\frac{P_{\text{Glow}}}{V_{\text{Glow}}}
=
\frac{1.2P}{\frac43 V}
=
1.2 \times \frac34 \times \frac{P}{V}
=
0.9 \times 1.00
=
0.90
\]

So Glow costs \(\$0.90\) per unit volume, or \(90\) cents.

The answer is 90.
